name: Flo
tagline: Period, ovulation and symptom tracker with cycle predictions, health content and a paid premium tier.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip away the content library and the core of Flo is a date log plus arithmetic: average cycle length, average period length, next predicted start, a fertile window guess. An agent can produce a local-first PWA that does exactly that in one session, and because the data never leaves your phone it is arguably the more private option. What you cannot one-shot is the editorial machine: thousands of reviewed articles, symptom explainers, pregnancy mode, the chat assistant, and prediction models tuned on an enormous anonymized cycle corpus. For most people the prediction delta between a good average and a trained model is small enough that nobody notices. The honest catch is habit: a tracker you forget to open is worse than a mediocre one with a push notification.
coreLoopDIY: Log period start and end dates plus daily symptoms on a calendar, and get a predicted next start, period window and estimated fertile window computed from your own history.
requirements: A phone that can install a PWA, or any browser
Static hosting or just running it locally
Willingness to export your own backup file, since there is no cloud sync
whatYouLose: The content library: symptom explainers, health articles, pregnancy and menopause modes
Predictions informed by a huge anonymized cycle dataset rather than only your last six cycles
Reliable push reminders and a polished native app your partner can also be looped into
Apple Health and Google Fit sync, plus automatic backup and device migration
The in-app assistant and anything resembling clinically reviewed guidance
moatNotes: The dataset genuinely improves predictions at the margins, but the bigger asset is being the app hundreds of millions of people already trust with the single most sensitive category of health data.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because cycle tracking is a daily habit app, and habit apps win on polish, reminders and not having to think. Flo also sells reassurance: curated answers to anxious questions at 2am, pregnancy mode, symptom context written by people with credentials. A self-built tracker gives you the numbers and nothing else, which is fine if the numbers are all you wanted and quietly insufficient if they were not.
notes: The prediction math is a weekend of high school statistics; the trust is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first period and cycle tracking PWA called "Cycle". Nothing leaves the device.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all storage
- vite-plugin-pwa for installability and offline use
- date-fns for date math
- No backend, no accounts, no analytics, no network calls at all

Data model in Dexie:
- cycles: id, startDate, endDate (nullable while ongoing)
- logs: id, date, flow (none/light/medium/heavy), symptoms (string array), mood, notes
- settings: default cycle length, default period length, reminder lead days

Features, in scope:
- A month calendar as the home screen. Past period days filled, predicted period days outlined, estimated fertile window and predicted ovulation day shaded differently.
- Big primary button: "Period started today" / "Period ended today", context aware.
- Tap any day to open a log sheet: flow, multi-select symptoms from a fixed list (cramps, headache, bloating, acne, fatigue, tender breasts, nausea), mood, free text note.
- Stats view: average cycle length, average period length, shortest and longest cycle, variability, and the last twelve cycles as a simple bar chart. Say plainly when there is not enough history yet.
- Prediction: mean of the last six completed cycles, falling back to the settings default when there are fewer than three. Show predictions as ranges, not single dates, and label them estimates.
- Settings: export all data as JSON, import it back, wipe everything with a confirm step.
- Optional local notification via the Notifications API when an installed PWA, reminding N days before a predicted start. Degrade silently if unsupported.

Out of scope, do not build: cloud sync, login, sharing, pregnancy mode, health articles, any AI chat, any third party SDK.

UI: mobile-first, thumb-reachable, large tap targets, dark mode by default, no onboarding carousel. Seed a dev-only fixture of nine plausible past cycles behind a flag so the calendar and stats are not empty on first run. Write a README covering install as a PWA, the backup/export routine, and a one paragraph note that predictions are statistical estimates and not contraception.
